title: Mixed Numbers and Fractions Greater Than 1
trouble: Children convert 2 1/3 to 3/3 by multiplying only the whole number or adding 2 + 1.

blocks.html: You know that whole numbers can be written as fractions ($1 = \dfrac{3}{3}$, $2 = \dfrac{6}{3}$) and how to add like fractions. Put those together and an amount bigger than 1 can be written two ways.

$2\dfrac{1}{3}$ (a mixed number) and $\dfrac{7}{3}$ (a fraction greater than 1) name the same amount. Mixed to fraction: wholes × denominator, plus the numerator: $2 \times 3 + 1 = 7$, so $\dfrac{7}{3}$. Fraction to mixed: divide, $7 \div 3 = 2$ R 1, so $2\dfrac{1}{3}$.

Each whole is 3 thirds. Two wholes are $3 + 3 = 6$ thirds, and the extra $\dfrac{1}{3}$ makes 7 thirds. Going back, every 3 thirds you can group make one whole; 7 thirds make 2 groups with 1 third left over.

blocks.name: fractioncircle
blocks.cap: $\dfrac{7}{3}$: two full circles of thirds and one more third. That is $2\dfrac{1}{3}$.

blocks.title: Mixed number to fraction
steps: Each whole is 5 fifths, so 3 wholes are $3 \times 5 = 15$ fifths.

blocks.title: Fraction to mixed number
steps: How many groups of 4 fourths are in 11 fourths? $11 \div 4 = 2$ R 3.

blocks.html: Multiplying only the whole number ($3 \times 2 = 6$, so "$\dfrac{6}{5}$") or just adding $3 + 2$. The wholes must be turned into fifths first: 3 wholes are 15 fifths, then add the 2 fifths. Check: $\dfrac{17}{5}$ is a bit more than $\dfrac{15}{5} = 3$.
